_comment: How each people builds (realmwalker/world/towns). sizes: the close-up map of each kind of place, [width, height] in squares ('great': the one or two greatest cities of a world). great: how many great cities a world has (small, medium, large worlds) and how many times bigger they are than the other cities. styles: per people (a culture's 'town' in cultures.json). layout: the plan of the place: organic (roads in from the country to a market square), grid (planned blocks round a square), medina (a bazaar street, winding alleys, courtyard houses), camp (rings of tents round a great tent), kremlin (a wooden fort with its church, log houses outside), terraces (white houses stepping down a slope), plaza (a stepped pyramid on a great plaza, causeways, thatched compounds), longhouse (long halls round a mead hall inside an earth bank), hold (cut into the rock), grove (homes in giant trees), burrows (homes dug into green mounds), stockade (huts in a ring of stakes). street, lane: the ground of the main streets and the alleys; plaza: the ground of the square. wall, palisade: what a walled town (or a walled village) is walled with. look: per kind of building ('_' for any other): [roof, walls, shape] choices, roof and walls naming pictures in ui/gfx/roofs.py, shape one of rect, round, long, court, tree, mound. floor: the floor inside. square: the things in the middle of the place. street_things: what stands about the streets. trees: what grows between the houses. light: what lights the streets at night (lamp_post, brazier, lantern, torch_post). extra: special buildings this people's bigger places have.

approach: The road climbs into {name} between dry-stone dykes thick with moss.
{name} huddles in the lee of the hill, folk and cattle under the same long roofs.
Shaggy red cattle watch you come up the track into {name}.
You come into {name} over a stone bridge where the burn runs brown with peat.
sight: Peat smoke seeps out through the thatch; there is not a chimney in the place.
Somebody is practising the pipes, badly, the same four notes over and over.
Plaids in the clan's colours dry on the heather by the doors.
Men in kilts haul stones for a new dyke, arguing about where it should go.
smell: It smells of peat smoke, wet wool and cattle.
The air is sharp with peat reek and the mash of a still somewhere.
detail: A standing stone older than the clan leans by the well.
The skull of a great stag is nailed over the chieftain's door.
Children stop a game of shinty to stare at you, sticks in hand.
A cairn by the road has a fresh stone on top of it.

approach: The way into {name} runs between turf banks and racks of drying fish.
Longships lie hauled up on the shingle below {name}, their dragon heads unshipped.
You come into {name} past a runestone painted red and black.
{name} is a cluster of long, low halls, their turf roofs green as the hills.
sight: Smoke leaks from the ridge of the mead hall; someone inside is singing.
Men split wood in the yard, bare-armed in the cold, their breath steaming.
A woman with a ring of keys at her belt is shouting at a thrall.
Shields hang along the hall's wall, each painted with its own beast.
smell: It smells of tar, fish and woodsmoke.
The air smells of salt, smoke and wet dog.
detail: A horse skull grins from a pole at the edge of the place.
Two thralls are mending a net as long as a house.
Boys wrestle in the mud while the old men judge the falls.
Somebody has carved a ship on the doorpost, with a name in runes beneath it.

approach: The road into {name} runs between olive groves and white walls.
{name} climbs its hill in terraces of red-tiled roofs.
A bell tower rises over {name}, long before you see the town itself.
You come into {name} under an arch with a saint carved into its keystone.
sight: Old women in black sit in a doorway's shade, missing nothing.
Washing hangs across the lanes from balcony to balcony.
A fountain splashes in the square, and mules drink from its trough.
Men play cards under the arcade and pretend not to look at you.
smell: It smells of hot stone, olive oil and garlic.
The air smells of oranges, dust and bread.
detail: The temple doors are carved with saints whose faces have been rubbed smooth by hands.
Dogs sleep in the shade of the arcades and will not move for anyone.
Somewhere a lute is being tuned, and tuned again.
A procession's paper flowers still hang, faded, from the balconies.

approach: {name} spills down to its harbour in white houses and blue doors.
The road into {name} passes marble tombs, their inscriptions worn to whispers.
Fishing boats with eyes painted on their prows crowd the harbour of {name}.
You come into {name} along a colonnade where the columns do not all match.
sight: Men argue philosophy, or the price of fish, under the colonnade.
Amphorae are stacked like firewood along the quay.
A marble statue in the square has lost its nose and gained a gull.
Sponge divers sit drying in the sun, their ears ruined by the deep.
smell: It smells of salt, pine resin and grilled octopus.
The air smells of thyme, tar and the sea.
detail: Offerings hang at a roadside shrine: little tin hands, eyes, a leg.
An olive press creaks as a blindfolded donkey walks its endless circle.
A cat sleeps on every warm step.
A herald reads out the council's decree to a crowd that is not listening.

approach: The road into {name} passes palms and a well where camels kneel to drink.
{name} rises out of the heat haze, its walls the colour of the sand.
You come into {name} through a gate whose tiles are blue as deep water.
A caravan is unloading at the gate of {name}, bales and bells and shouting.
sight: The call to prayer drifts over the flat roofs.
In the bazaar, merchants sit cross-legged among their carpets and their brass.
Lattice windows look down on the alley; someone behind one is watching you.
A water-seller's cups chime as he walks.
smell: It smells of cumin, cardamom and dust.
The air is heavy with incense, dung smoke and roasting almonds.
detail: Water runs in a narrow channel down the middle of the street.
A storyteller holds a crowd in the shade of the gate.
Every door is a different colour, and every one of them is shut.
Verses are written in tiles over the fountain, in a script that flows like water.

approach: Horses graze for a mile around {name} before you see the first tent.
Smoke rises from a hundred felt tents where {name} has pitched this season.
Riders come out to look you over before you reach {name}, then gallop back without a word.
The grass round {name} is cropped to the roots by the herds.
sight: Horse-tail standards stir in the wind before the khan's great white tent.
Children too young to walk well ride bareback between the tents.
Women milk mares, and the milk goes into great leather bags to sour.
Each clan's tents stand in a ring round its own fire, doors facing in.
smell: It smells of horses, dung fires and sour milk.
The air smells of smoke, mutton fat and wind.
detail: A shaman's tent stands apart, hung with bells and ribbons.
Carts with tents still lashed to them wait to move at a word.
An eagle on a man's fist turns its head to watch you pass.
Nothing here is built to stay: by the next moon it could all be gone.

approach: The road into {name} is laid with logs, and the logs bounce under the wheels.
Golden onion domes rise over {name} long before you reach its walls.
{name} stands behind a stockade of sharpened logs on a bluff above the river.
You come into {name} past a roadside shrine with a little roof against the snow.
sight: Carved window frames are painted blue and red against the grey of the logs.
A bell rings out from the domed temple, and people stop to bow.
Boardwalks run between the houses over mud that never quite dries.
A sledge loaded with furs is dragged towards the fort.
smell: It smells of birch smoke, tar and cabbage soup.
The air smells of rye bread and wet timber.
detail: A bathhouse by the river steams; someone runs out of it and straight into the water.
Bears' hides are stretched to dry along the stockade.
An old woman sells sunflower seeds from a sack, spitting the husks.
Every gable ends in a carved horse's head.

approach: A causeway leads into {name} across fields of maize and beans.
The stepped pyramid of {name} rises over the trees, smoke rising from its top.
You come into {name} past ball-court walls carved with skulls.
Canoes slide along the canals of {name}, low with fruit and flowers.
sight: Priests with painted faces climb the long stair of the pyramid.
Market women sell cacao, peppers and bright feathers from mats in the plaza.
Conch trumpets sound from the temple, and the plaza falls quiet.
Warriors in jaguar skins lounge by the temple stair.
smell: It smells of copal smoke, maize cakes and hot stone.
The air smells of flowers, rot and smoke.
detail: A rack of skulls stands by the foot of the temple stair.
Canals of green water run between the house gardens.
Every doorway has its little altar: a flower, a cup, a tiny clay god.
A ballgame is being played; the crowd's roar rolls across the plaza.

approach: The path into {name} winds between trees older than any kingdom.
Lanterns hang in the branches over the way into {name}, glowing without flame.
There is no gate to {name}; you only notice, after a while, that the trees have doors.
The forest grows quiet as you come into {name}, as if it were listening.
sight: The homes are grown, not built: living trunks swollen into halls.
Music drifts down from the high branches, in no key you know.
The pool in the glade glows faintly, even by day.
Pale figures move between the trees and are gone before you can count them.
smell: It smells of moss, rain and blossom.
The air smells of green wood and something like honey.
detail: Nobody seems to look at you, and yet everyone knows you are here.
A white deer drinks at the moonwell and does not startle.
The bark of the oldest tree is carved with names in a flowing hand.
Leaves fall here in every season, and none of them lie on the paths.

approach: The road climbs to the gate of {name}, cut into the cliff between two stone kings.
Great doors of iron-bound stone stand open in the mountainside.
The way up to {name} passes slag heaps, and smoke rises from vents high on the mountain.
Bearded wardens in mail watch the road to {name} from slits in the rock.
sight: Galleries run away into the dark, a brazier burning at every turning.
The hammering of a hundred forges echoes through the halls.
Carved ancestors stand along the high road, each as tall as three men.
Ore carts rumble past, pushed by dwarves who do not look up.
smell: It smells of hot iron, coal smoke and stone dust.
The air is warm and smells of beer and forge fires.
detail: The rails of the ore carts are worn bright down the middle of the gallery.
Runes over every door name the clan within and its trade.
Somewhere below, water drips into a dark lake.
It is the same hour in here at noon as at midnight: the fires decide when it is day.

approach: The lane into {name} winds between hedges and round green doors.
{name} is hard to see at first: its houses are inside the hills.
Fat ponies graze the paddocks along the road into {name}.
You come into {name} past an orchard where somebody is asleep under a tree.
sight: Smoke curls up from chimney pots that stick out of the grass.
Every round window has a pot of flowers in it.
The party tree on the green is still hung with lanterns from the last feast.
Gardeners kneel among the cabbages, comparing marrows.
smell: It smells of pipe-weed, apples and baking.
The air smells of bacon and new-mown hay.
detail: A notice on the party tree announces a birthday and a feast, everyone welcome.
Nobody here is in a hurry, least of all the postmaster.
Children chase a pig through somebody's garden, to loud complaint.
Every door is round, and every one of them is painted a different colour.

approach: The way into {name} is lined with stakes, and some of the stakes have heads on them.
{name} squats behind a ditch and a ring of sharpened logs.
Dogs the size of wolves come out to bark at you long before you reach {name}.
You come into {name} past a midden heap the size of a hill.
sight: Huts of hide and bone crowd round a great fire pit.
War banners hang from their poles, stiff with old blood.
Two warriors fight in the mud while the others bet on them.
A shaman daubs the doorposts with something red.
smell: It smells of smoke, blood and rancid fat.
The air reeks of tanning hides and the latrine ditch.
detail: A drum beats somewhere, slow, like a heart.
Trophies hang over the chief's hut: shields, skulls, half a crown.
The ground near the fire is black with the fat of old feasts.
Somebody has carved a crude likeness of the chief, and somebody else has defaced it.
